findings.reason: the plan must either wire the interface-budget item into the prompt, the item set and the parser, or delete §3's second done-when; as written it promises a check no reviewer is asked to make.
findings.text: §3's second "also done when" requires the review to name the current week's four interface counts from reckon/interface_counts.py and to raise a finding when a section adds a public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family without retiring or merging something, but the design-review prompt and PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS (reckon/crew/review.py:157) carry only the four reuse/depth items and no code path injects the counts into the brief — interface_counts.py's own docstring already claims its four families are "the ones the plan-review rubric reads" as a reader that does not exist

findings.reason: the plan should name reckon/crew/review.py as the owner of the sibling-path rule and have plan_review extend it, so a future change to the store's keying lands once rather than diverging silently.
findings.text: plan_review_path rebuilds the "plain path plus .at-<sha> sibling when one version is reviewed twice" scheme that reckon/crew/review.py:1215 review_path already owns, with its own _BLOB_RE and its own suffix spelling, so the store's keying rule lives in two places and would have to be changed in both

findings.reason: §12(a) must direct the census to import the pattern from reckon/crew/plan_review.py (the module that owns the store's filename grammar) instead of hardcoding it, or the two globs drift again the moment one is edited.
findings.text: directory_counts globs `plan-*.json` itself while the reader it is meant to be reconciled against, plan_review.list_plan_reviews (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:548), owns the `plan-*.v*.json` spelling, and §12(a) says the fix will "use the reader's own plan-*.v*.json pattern" without naming an owner to extend — so as specified §12(a) re-spells a second literal rather than removing the duplicate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — reckon/crew/plan_review.py hides the record shape, the content fingerprint, the store, responses, recurrence and the delivered-report join behind a small public API, and shares the report reader with review.py through parse_plan_review_report rather than duplicating it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — plan_review.plan_review_path re-implements review.py's blob-keyed sibling path, and the census script re-implements the store's plan-file glob rather than reading either from its owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 cites reckon/interface_counts.py as the source of the interface budget the review reads, but the shipped design-review prompt (reckon/crew/prompts/plan_design_review.md) and PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS (reckon/crew/review.py:157) never read those counts or ask for them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan extends the existing review store and the review-dispatch reflex (recovery._review_dispatch_fields carries both the run subject and the plan subject) instead of wrapping them, so D6's extend-not-copy is realised in the code.
